comments: NGC5584 is a newly added SN Ia host. Figure 7 lists 94 measured Cepheids, but the post-rejection count is not reported. Its metallicity gradient is included in the simultaneous Wesenheit fit.
Pure theoretical F160W PL fit for Z=0.02, Y=0.28 and P>10 d. The 78 good Cepheids define the fit; sigma=0.32 mag. The quoted error is only the standard error of the mean.
NGC 5584 result from Table 5. Approximate SN-independent distance using the metallicity-dependent NIR Wesenheit global solution.
LMC-calibrated alternative without metallicity correction. It is 0.147+/-0.060 mag below the cited SH0ES value and is considered less suitable because of the LMC-NGC 5584 metallicity mismatch.
Preferred solution using the Galactic Wesenheit PL calibration. No explicit metallicity correction is applied because the MW and NGC 5584 have similar metallicities.
Preferred SN-independent mu_host. The common systematic term is correlated and should not be added independently for different hosts. Error computed/retrieved from Table6.
Approximate mu_Ceph obtained after excluding only SN 2007af. The final sample contains 165 globally fitted Cepheids. Error computed/retrieved from Table6.
First TRGB distance for NGC 5584. The listed error is random; an additional 0.12 mag systematic applies. Blue RGB selection minimizes crowding and host extinction, which is assumed negligible.
Preferred combined-anchor QT solution from the lowest-sky region. A 0.006 mag artificial-star offset was applied. Error is random only; systematic=0.057 mag.
Combined-anchor blue-I solution from uniformly reprocessed HST/ACS photometry in the lowest-sky region. Error is random only; the common systematic is 0.057 mag.
Preliminary JWST result using a method-matched unweighted Sobel calibration from NGC4258. A secondary edge lies about 0.1 mag fainter, but artificial-star bias is below 0.01 mag.
Baseline s=0.05 mag smoothing selects the brighter of two nearly equal Sobel peaks. Add sigma_var=0.07 mag for peak choices; the 0.032 mag maser uncertainty is excluded.
Alternative s=0.10 mag smoothing selects the fainter Sobel peak and raises mu_0 by 0.15 mag. Add sigma_var=0.07 mag; the 0.032 mag maser uncertainty is excluded.
